about.bio: I'm a computer science major at Michigan State with a curiosity for how things work. I dabble in user interface design and learn Swift in my free time.
about.bioExtra: I build intuitive software that integrates into one's life. I believe in algorithms over opinions and testing multiple approaches to find the best fit. As a fast learner with a sharp eye for detail, I look for perfection in executing my ideas.

opensource.title: Open-Source Philosophy
opensource.paragraph1: Releasing old proprietary code into the open-source ecosystem creates new life into retired projects. Instead of letting software sit idle on a private hard drive, sharing it to the public gives a chance for others to learn, fix bugs, and even develop new tools. As a developer, I am constantly making tools for myself, and open-sourcing them is the absolute best way for others facing the same problems to actually find them.
opensource.paragraph2: Equally important is the practice of open-sourcing the small, non-commercial tools I build every day. These highly specific utilities are created strictly for my own needs to scratch my own operational itches. They aren't meant for production or profit. Still, for businesses, adopting this model of open-sourcing some of their work promotes transparency and encourages workflows where minor internal utilities can be rapidly created and shared. Sharing these scripts creates unexpected collaboration, showcases practical engineering, and builds trust through total transparency.
